conclusion: Channel growth is hit-concentrated: top video = 13-78% of channel views
A hit does not raise the channel floor (SHH 9,539 -> 9,418 median; Okoro recent-10 median 75)
Same title on a different channel yields radically different results (2 to 1.6M); same persona + identical title + identical thumbnail (incl. typo) 5 days apart: 941,154 vs 160
Cohort channels share packaging but not scripts (max cross-channel transcript 5-gram Jaccard 0.024)
Ares and Elias show same-operator signals (identical thumbnail text incl. typos, same mismatched thumbnail on a different title)

Copy outcome depends on the copying channel, not order: across 37 cross-channel same-title pairs second movers won 22; at >=29 days they won 14/16 (stronger channels re-running weak channels' titles); inside the Ares-Elias twin, re-runs >=15 days later lost 4/6
Thumbnails that withhold the answer outperform those that reveal it (1.90x vs 0.47x; 0/14 revealed reached 3x)
Warning-hook openings and warning icons underperform within channel (0.32x hooks, 14 of 22 below 0.5x; 0.55x icons)
Many large winners had little or no web-search demand at upload (bathing 0/100, eyesight 0, anesthesia dip) - discovery appears non-search
Trend alignment helped some winners (neuropathy peak week; garlic Jan peak; clove multi-year rise) but high interest did not rescue losers (stroke Jun 2026, sleeping-position Okoro)
Generic stroke warning content failed on all 3 channels that ran it
Conditional audience gating is not fatal (eggs-if-diabetes 127.6K) - pass-1 '247x from narrowing' over-attributed
Series/franchise behavior drives the largest absolute results (SHH: 41 clove entries = 73.1% of channel views, 14 of 41 >=3x; exact repeats of the 3.09M format returned to ~1x)
Winning openings place the viewer inside a lived moment within ~20 s and set an open loop within ~100 s
Several category winners carry unsupported medical claims; performance lessons must be separated from the claims
AI-assisted production is disclosed in 26/32 Aliza transcripts; composite patients disclosed
Small channels can break out quickly (Aliza persona channel, Okoro, Fit Lit - the latter serves a South-Asian-language audience), usually on proven topics with new packaging
Whitespace with rising demand and no cohort coverage: GLP-1 brand shift, creatine, BP-timing trial, mini-stroke in women, supplement interactions
